scoreScale: 0.00 to 1.00, where higher means stronger strategic alignment rather than probability.

Vanguard Pressure.tooltip: Occupy the front early and make blockers insufficient.
Vanguard Pressure.description: Honest board pressure from cheap and mid-cost bodies, token turns, charge/burst, and site attacks. The deck wins by forcing repeated combat rather than mostly bypassing blockers.

subStyles.Board Beatdown: Efficient bodies and combat tricks create steady, honest pressure.
subStyles.Burn Pressure: Board damage is backed by direct damage and Death's Door finishers.
subStyles.Token Vanguard: Token production and anthem effects flood the vanguard.
subStyles.Site-Race Pressure: The deck prioritizes damaging sites and forcing Death's Door quickly.

Evasive Aggro.tooltip: Kill through hard-to-block damage and awkward attack lanes.
Evasive Aggro.description: Airborne, Stealth, Voidwalk, Submerge, Burrowing, or other evasive angles let threats ignore normal blocking patterns and pressure Avatars or Sites quickly.

subStyles.Airborne Pressure: Airborne bodies and air mobility carry the damage plan.
subStyles.Voidwalk Pressure: Voidwalk threats attack from the void or strange board positions.
subStyles.Stealth/Infiltrate: Stealth and control-their-minion effects create unblockable tempo swings.
subStyles.Submerge Pressure: Submerge bodies hide from normal interaction and surface to attack.

Mobility Control.tooltip: Make combat happen in the wrong place for the opponent.
Mobility Control.description: Push, pull, swap, teleport, submerge, bury, drown, force attacks, or otherwise reposition units so the opponent cannot use their board efficiently.

subStyles.Drown/Displacement: Water and forced movement repeatedly convert positioning into removal.
subStyles.Tempo Displacement: Push, pull, swap, and bounce effects create tempo wins rather than hard locks.
subStyles.Kiting Control: Ranged/projectile threats and movement keep combat one-sided.
subStyles.Tap/Disable Control: Disable, silence, immobile, and tap effects prevent enemy threats from acting.

Fortress Control.tooltip: Turn Sites into a defensive realm, not just mana.
Fortress Control.description: Defensive Sites, walls, chokepoints, big blockers, healing, Ward, and repeated board wipes make attacks inefficient until the control deck can win safely.

subStyles.Defensive Realm: The Atlas is used to slow paths and protect important squares.
subStyles.Terrain Prison: Terrain and auras restrict movement, attacks, or access to key regions.
subStyles.Ward/Heal Fortress: Healing, Ward, and protection effects stretch the game until threats take over.

Champion Threat.tooltip: One central unit or Avatar becomes the main weapon.
Champion Threat.description: The Avatar or a single central threat is equipped, protected, moved, and repeatedly used to attack or control the board.

subStyles.Armed Avatar: Artifacts, weapons, and bearer buffs make the Avatar a primary attacker.
subStyles.Mobile Champion: Movement and reach effects keep the champion in the right fight.
subStyles.Protected Champion: Ward, healing, bodyguards, or prevention keep the main threat alive.

Sticky Recursion.tooltip: Trade, die, return, and grind through removal.
Sticky Recursion.description: The deck converts death and the cemetery into board presence, tokens, Genesis re-use, or repeatable value so clean answers are hard to maintain.

subStyles.Necro Value: Skeletons, dead minions, and reanimation effects supply repeatable board presence.
subStyles.Deathspeaker Genesis: Dead Genesis minions are copied or replayed for value.
subStyles.Sacrifice/Deathrite: Sacrifice, Deathrite, and death triggers turn trades into resources.

Realm Denial.tooltip: Stop the opponent using their Realm properly.
Realm Denial.description: Destroy, replace, disable, flood, bury, or punish Sites; interfere with threshold and Atlas plans; or block paths so the opponent's mana and movement collapse.

subStyles.Threshold Denial: The deck attacks threshold, mana, or site text.
subStyles.Site Destruction: The deck destroys, replaces, or banishes Sites.
subStyles.Path Denial: Sites and terrain block movement or create pathing traps.

Resource Engine Midrange.tooltip: Out-scale with ramp, Atlas economy, card flow, and high-rate threats.
Resource Engine Midrange.description: A broad value style for decks whose main edge is resource production, site economy, tutors, draw, ramp, and efficient threats rather than a single pure aggro or control axis.

subStyles.Ramp Midrange: Site acceleration and mana engines reach large threats early.
subStyles.Toolbox Goodstuff: Collection access, tutors, and flexible answers carry the deck.
subStyles.Atlas Value: The Atlas is an engine for mana, bodies, or repeated utility.

Spell Engine Control.tooltip: Survive, loop or chain spells, then win by inevitability.
Spell Engine Control.description: High spell density, tutoring, spell copying, recasting, board wipes, and card flow create a long-game control shell that wins once resources are exhausted.

subStyles.Archimago Loop: Repeated casting or copying of key spells is central to the plan.
subStyles.Removal-Heavy Control: Removal and sweepers dominate until a finisher appears.
subStyles.Tutor/Cantrip Control: Search, draw, cantrips, and selection are the core engine.

Unknown.tooltip: No stable style signature was strong enough.
Unknown.description: Used only when the deck has too little information, is an unusual pile, or has no clear common strategic cluster.

subStyles.Unclear: No single style signature dominates from the card mix.

scoringNotes.cardScoring: Derived from type, rules text keywords, stats/cost, and a small popularity tie-breaker from deck occurrence in the archive.
scoringNotes.deckScoring: Aggregates package scores from Spellbook, Atlas, and Collection with lower weight for Collection and minimal weight for Maybe; then adds small Avatar and primer/name priors.
scoringNotes.styleScores: Style scores are independent affinity scores; they are not normalized to sum to 1. A deck can strongly align with multiple styles.
scoringNotes.unknown: Unknown is assigned only when all style affinities are weak.
